original_metadata.title: Freiheitssatz for unital generic Poisson algebras over any characteristic-zero field, with anticommutative Leibniz bracket and no Jacobi identity
original_metadata.author: Pavel S. Kolesnikov; Leonid G. Makar-Limanov; Ivan P. Shestakov
original_metadata.source_title: The Freiheitssatz for Generic Poisson Algebras
original_metadata.difficulty_reason: The proof constructs conditionally closed generic Poisson algebras through a differential-field functor with explicitly noncommuting twisted derivations. Its essential new core classifies multiderivation polynomials in the free anticommutative algebra using flip symmetries and primitive enveloping-algebra elements, then reduces all polynomial identities to that form and separates them by an explicit evaluation.

proof_review.note: Read full unlabelled Theorem3 and its entire essential new chain: conditionally-closed functor Proposition1 and Freiheitssatz Lemma1, flips and primitive-operator Lemmas2-5/Theorem1, Farkas-height reduction Proposition2, Jacobian factorization Proposition3 and separating evaluations Proposition4. Ground field characteristiczero; generic Poisson means unital associative commutative product and anticommutative Leibniz bracket, without Jacobi. For f depending on the extra free generatorx, the ideal(f) has zero intersection with the free algebra on the remaining generators. Differential-field closure Theorem2 is explicitly a known theorem from Kolchin/Ritt, with an author sketch; it is cited established background, not an unexpanded new core. The source provides all new constructions and evaluation argument. Ordinary Poisson/Jordan corollaries and Jacobian classification helpers are not separately counted.

original_metadata.statement_scope: Full unlabelled Theorem3 with its precise Section2 Freiheitssatz formulation: for X countable,x outsideX and f in GP(X union{x}) outsideGP(X), ideal(f) intersectsGP(X) trivially over a characteristic-zero field. Generic Poisson bracket is not assumed Jacobi. The editorial locator t3 is not an original TeX label.
